children: The company plans to deploy Rs 132 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue towards marketing and business promotion for its marketplace business

AceVector, the parent company of Snapdeal and Unicommerce eSolutions, has fixed the price band for its initial public offering (IPO) at Rs 30-32 per equity share, with the issue set to open for subscription on September 25 and close on September 29.
The Kunal Bahl and Rohit Kumar Bansal-promoted company, which counts SoftBank among its investors, is targeting a total issue size of Rs 420 crore at the upper end of the price band.
The anchor investor portion will open on September 24. At the upper end of the price band, AceVector is expected to have a post-issue market capitalisation of around Rs 1,741.4 crore.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 133 crore. The shares have a face value of Rs 1 each.

Existing investors, including SoftBank subsidiary Starfish and Nexus Venture Partners, will participate in the OFS. Other selling shareholders include FIH Business Global, Kenneth Stuart Glass, Jason Ashok Kothari, Rupen Investment and Industries, Centaurus Trading and Investments, and Laurent Bernard Amouyal.

Starfish is currently AceVector’s largest shareholder with a 30.11 per cent stake. Bahl holds 12.19 per cent, while Bansal owns 10.93 per cent. B2 Professional Services LLP, owned by the wives of Bahl and Bansal, holds another 10.87 per cent.
How AceVector Plans To Use IPO Proceeds

Of the total issue, 75 per cent has been reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), while non-institutional investors (NIIs) will be allocated 15 per cent. The remaining 10 per cent will be reserved for retail investors.
AceVector has already raised Rs 13 crore through a pre-IPO placement, with the proceeds set to be adjusted against the fresh issue.

The company plans to deploy Rs 132 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue towards marketing and business promotion for its marketplace business. Another Rs 50 crore has been earmarked for technology infrastructure for the marketplace business.
The remaining proceeds will be used for inorganic growth, including acquisitions, and general corporate purposes.

Gurugram-headquartered AceVector operates an asset-light digital commerce ecosystem comprising value-focused e-commerce marketplace Snapdeal, e-commerce enablement software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform Unicommerce eSolutions and consumer brands housed under Stellaro Brands.
The company continues to report losses, although its deficit narrowed in financial year 2026. Net loss stood at Rs 60.7 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 139.2 crore in the previous financial year.
Revenue from operations, meanwhile, increased 29.2 per cent to Rs 510.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 395 crore a year earlier.
IIFL Capital Services, CLSA India and Systematix Corporate Services have been appointed as the merchant bankers to the issue.
